claims.text: A blog post titled "SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi" exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ and covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration to Pulumi.
AWS CDK ties infrastructure to AWS only and is AWS-centric.
AWS CDK allows developers to define infrastructure using only TypeScript or Python.
SST Ion is the code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications, deployed using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation, and once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
Pulumi supports AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-prem.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK because CloudFormation is slower.
AWS CDK secrets management is limited to AWS Secrets Manager only.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C#.
A Founding Engineer at SST said Pulumi deployment feels like a natural extension of writing code.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` needs no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account, not Pulumi Cloud.
SST v3 is the Ion-based rewrite of SST.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps define infrastructure in a single `sst.config.ts` file and `sst deploy` provisions end to end.
Through 2023, SST's provisioning layer was built directly on AWS CDK and CloudFormation.
In late 2023 the SST team began a rewrite code-named Ion that replaced the entire deployment layer.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'When you run `sst deploy`, those resources make a call to an embedded Pulumi engine that makes a call to their bridged Terraform provider, and this makes the AWS SDK calls to create your resources.'
SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'
SST's platform/package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and others, and the Pulumiverse Vercel provider.
The SST repository is anomalyco/sst, formerly sst/sst.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge (pulumi-terraform-bridge) is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API works by embedding Pulumi programs inside other tools.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`, per its README.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed in the same SST app.
SST does not invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package had roughly 796,000 (796,291) weekly downloads for September 5-11, 2026.
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has more GitHub stars than SST.
Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components offer cross-team visibility, central guardrails, and shared infrastructure patterns.
opencode's growth hasn't changed SST's release cadence.
